jorge: Opening thread for PR #6999 — onprem: SUSE-specific networking notes + HSM pin-cache guidance + airgap cert rotation steps. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/6999

elaine: skimmed. main SUSE note: network scripts on older SLES use wicked rather than NetworkManager; need a short note telling operators to translate MTU and DNS steps for wicked. also mention SUSE default AppArmor profile that can block PKCS11 tools.

tim-d: good catch. I'll add a 2-line example for wicked: 
```
# set MTU on SLES wicked
wicked ifup eth0 MTU=1400
```
and a pointer to `apparmor_parser -r` to reload profiles if customers change rules for pkcs11 helper.

maya: for HSMs let's include a secure-PIN-cache recommendation: use a short-lived token file with 0600 and systemd-tmpfile.d config. show systemd snippet that writes token on boot and expires it after X minutes. keeps interactions airgapped-friendly.

infra-max: I'll draft the systemd tmpfile + timer. quick example: 
```
# /etc/tmpfiles.d/rw-hsm.conf
f /var/run/rw/hsm.pin 0600 root root - - "${PIN_FROM_ADMIN}"
# /etc/systemd/system/rw-hsm-expire.service
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'sleep 120; rm -f /var/run/rw/hsm.pin'
```
Note: docs should warn about operator PIN handling policies for compliance.

jorge: there's a small migration note: customers upgrading from older onprem installers to the minimal profile lose package opensc by default. add an install hint: `zypper in opensc` and a short verification command `pkcs11-tool --list-slots`.

elaine: airgap cert rotation — the existing doc referenced /docs/airgap/rotate.md but that page is internal-only. need to point to the public mirror rotation guide and include a minimal checklist: snapshot mirror, sign new bundle, sync to offline site, reload services in correct order (kms -> agent -> onprem). I'll add steps and a sample ordering script.

maya: SDK snippets — I'd like a Python + Rust example in this PR (different from the JS/Go examples from previous thread). show reading token from a file and creating TLS connector with custom CA. keep them small.

tim-d: I'll add the Rust snippet using reqwest and rustls: 
```rust
use std::fs;
use reqwest::Client;
use reqwest::Certificate;
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
  let ca = fs::read("/etc/rw/ca.pem")?;
  let cert = Certificate::from_pem(&ca)?;
  let client = Client::builder().add_root_certificate(cert).build()?;
  let token = fs::read_to_string("/var/run/rw/kms.token")?;
  let res = client.post("https://kms.local/decrypt")
    .bearer_auth(token.trim())
    .body("{\"ciphertext\":\"...\"}")
    .send().await?;
  println!("{}", res.status());
  Ok(())
}
```

maya: Python snippet (sync requests) I'll add: 
```python
import requests
from pathlib import Path
ca = '/etc/rw/ca.pem'
token = Path('/var/run/rw/kms.token').read_text().strip()
resp = requests.post('https://kms.local/decrypt', headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}'}, verify=ca, json={'ciphertext':'...'})
print(resp.status_code)
```

jorge: conn-checker: rather than the previous openssl-only check, let's include a lightweight HSM enumeration step for offline sites (captures EACCES vs missing library): 
```
#!/bin/sh
set -e
HOST=${1:-kms.local}
CA=/etc/rw/ca.pem
TOKEN=/var/run/rw/kms.token
# basic TCP
nc -z -w5 $HOST 443 || { echo "tcp fail"; exit 2; }
# TLS
echo | openssl s_client -connect ${HOST}:443 -CAfile $CA >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "tls fail"; exit 3; }
# token present
[ -f $TOKEN ] || { echo "token missing"; exit 4; }
# HSM quick list
if command -v pkcs11-tool >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  pkcs11-tool --list-slots >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "pkcs11 access fail"
else
  echo "pkcs11-tool missing"
fi
echo "conn-check ok"
```
Keep it POSIX shell to maximize compatibility with SLES containers.

infra-max: will validate that pkcs11-tool is available in our minimal installer images and add a note about packaging on SLES (packaging name `opensc`). also adding firewall matrix: required egress 443 to kms (TCP), optional ntp (UDP 123), and metadata-service access when using cloud-connected deploys.

elaine: one more nit — avoid suggesting `nc` on airgapped minimal images where busybox-nc might be missing. add fallback using bash /dev/tcp: 
```
(</dev/tcp/$HOST/443) >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo ok || echo fail
```

tim-d: thanks — I'll include the fallback and a small note about busybox differences.
